title: Phosphor Terminal — System Boot Sequence
description: A pure-black cyberdeck slide that faithfully simulates a phosphor-green terminal boot log: ASCII-art logo header, bracketed timestamp prefixes on every log line, a scanline overlay for CRT texture, and a blinking cursor block at the last line — monospace type end to end, no exceptions.
philosophy: This template exists for the speaker who wants the audience to feel like they've cracked into something live. It rejects every modern UI affordance — no gradients, no icons, no rounded corners, no variable-weight fonts — because the illusion of a running terminal session collapses the moment a sans-serif sneaks in. Hierarchy is purely temporal: lines accumulate, the cursor waits, the amber error line is the only permitted deviation from phosphor green. It is built for dark rooms, high-contrast projectors, and moments where the boot sequence IS the drama.
goodFor: Cybersecurity or ethical-hacking keynote title slides
Dev-conference talks about low-level systems or OS internals
Single dramatic reveal beats timed to the blinking cursor
Game-jam, CTF, or hackathon opening presentations
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews requiring legible data labels
Investor pitch decks where brand polish signals credibility
Academic citation-dense slides with footnotes or references
Any context requiring brand typefaces or logo lockups
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide must feel like an intrusion — a system caught mid-boot, printing to screen in real time with no awareness of an audience. Compositional rhythm is strictly vertical and accumulative: the ASCII-art header carries all the visual drama a traditional hero image would, and the log lines beneath it are sparse, cold, and purposeful. Every element reinforces the illusion of live machine output. Avoid any softness, curvature, drop shadows, or modern UI affordance — the tension lives entirely in the blinking cursor suspended at the bottom, waiting.

examples.layoutNotes: Edge-to-edge black field — no outer margin, no softening; the terminal owns every pixel of the canvas. Top third is reserved for a multi-row ASCII-art logo block, horizontally centered and treated as the primary identity element in lieu of any typographic headline. Below it, five to seven bracketed timestamp-prefixed log lines stack flush-left in a single consistent prefix column, simulating live boot output. A blinking cursor block anchors the very last line at the bottom-left; a full-canvas scanline rule overlay sits above everything as a finishing CRT texture pass.

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a live system process mid-execution — terminal output accumulating with the cold inevitability of a machine that does not pause for the audience. Compositional rhythm is dense-linear and strictly left-anchored; all hierarchy emerges from temporal order alone, with a single amber warning line serving as the only accent beat punctuating the phosphor-green stream. Avoid anything that reads as intentionally designed — no spatial breathing, no grouped visual clusters, no softness or rounding anywhere in the composition.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed pure-black canvas with no outer margin band; a fixed ~6-character left gutter is reserved exclusively for bracketed timestamp and status-code prefixes on every content line. Body content occupies a single left-anchored column running to roughly 90% canvas width, structured as sequential log lines — repeated ASCII dash or equals characters serve as the only permitted section dividers. The final line terminates with a blinking cursor block flush to the last character of text; a low-opacity scanline overlay sits above all content layers to simulate CRT phosphor persistence. Slide identity is encoded as a log-header line at the top of the column, not as a separate title band or decorative chrome.
